source_freeze.purpose: Downstream heldout/Bumpy/Mystery source with actual jump-slot telemetry; original flat freeze preserved unchanged

scope: Three genuinely held-out seeds after seed101 selection. Original and continued checkpoints use identical corrected controller+driver+COM+torso physics and matched realized randomization. No robot claim.

metrics.scope: simulation only; measured velocities are simulator observations, not hardware speed

driver_target_contract.order: raw action retained; affine target; controller clamp; driver clamp; encoder-bias correction; actuator latency
driver_target_contract.scope: Position-command limits under active PD control; no claim about installed robot limits, measured torque or physical validation

locomotion_contact_contract.scope: Torso contacts terrain and nonadjacent active knee/foot spheres; no lower-leg hulls added. Original masses, sphere geometry and sphere collision properties retained.

domain_randomization.sampling: startup parameters are sampled once per world, not re-sampled each reset
domain_randomization.scope: initialized simulator fields; does not establish policy robustness or hardware transfer

collision_model.scope: actual compiled collision masks; disabled torso geometry can be measured diagnostically but contributes no contact response

provenance.randomized_flag_semantics: selects training task configuration; play configuration already retains startup physics randomization and observation noise

action_target_audit.meaning: raw actor actions; unclipped post-wrapper affine request; target_joint_pos after configured clip before latency/bias; physical_target_joint_pos subtracts bias before latency; actuator_input_target_joint_pos is post-step target after action-term latency/bias but before internal actuator delay (reset steps excluded); deployment target clamps affine request to model joint ranges; clipping fractions use unclipped request

limitations: Only three held-out randomization seeds; worlds/time samples are correlated.
The candidate was frozen before these results; no reselection or tuning against the holdouts.
A seed-level Pareto regression blocks general promotion even if average velocity error improves.
No physical performance or installed Pi contract is established.
decision: Retain as a research speed/stability candidate only; do not replace the deployed locomotion default. It removes all observed heldout failures and reduces mean XY error, but increases reverse torque/slip/yaw costs and fails the frozen promotion rule in every heldout seed.
